title: Swap Two Integers
description: A classic function that exchanges the values of two integers using pointers.
expected_explanation: This function swaps two integers by dereferencing pointers to access and modify the original values. It uses a temporary variable to hold one value while reassigning the other, then places the temp value in the second location. This works because pointers allow modification of values outside the function scope.

title: String Length
description: Calculate the length of a string by counting characters until the null terminator.
expected_explanation: This function iterates through a string using pointer arithmetic. It increments a counter each time it encounters a character, stopping when it reaches the null terminator ('\0'). The str++ advances the pointer to the next character in memory. It returns the total character count.

title: Memory Copy
description: Copy n bytes from source memory to destination memory.
expected_explanation: This function copies n bytes from source to destination by casting void pointers to char pointers (byte-level access). It iterates n times, copying each byte from source to destination. Void pointers are used to allow copying any data type. The char cast enables byte-by-byte copying.

title: Linked List Insert
description: Insert a new node at the beginning of a linked list.
expected_explanation: This function creates a new node by allocating memory with malloc, sets its data field, and links it to the current head. The new node's next pointer points to the old head, making it the new beginning of the list. This returns the new head for the caller to update their list reference.

title: Hash Table Lookup
description: Search for a value in a hash table using linear probing.
expected_explanation: This function uses modulo to compute an initial hash index, then performs linear probing to handle collisions. It loops through the table, checking each entry until finding the matching key or encountering an empty slot (key == 0). If found, it returns the associated value; otherwise returns -1 for not found.

title: Binary Search
description: Search for a value in a sorted array using divide-and-conquer.
expected_explanation: This function divides the search space in half each iteration using left and right pointers. It calculates mid position, compares the element there with the target, then eliminates half the remaining elements. This continues until the target is found or left > right, indicating the value doesn't exist. Time complexity is O(log n).

title: Bubble Sort
description: Sort an array using the bubble sort algorithm with swaps.
expected_explanation: This function repeatedly compares adjacent elements and swaps them if they're in wrong order. The outer loop controls passes, the inner loop performs comparisons. After each pass, the largest unsorted element 'bubbles' to its correct position at the end. The (n - i - 1) ensures we don't re-check sorted elements.

title: Simple Malloc Implementation
description: Allocate memory from a preallocated heap using a simple free list.
expected_explanation: This function walks a free list of memory blocks looking for one that's unallocated and large enough. When found, it marks the block as allocated and returns a pointer to the memory after the metadata (block + 1). The +1 pointer arithmetic skips the Block struct header. Returns NULL if no suitable block exists.

title: Binary Tree In-Order Traversal
description: Traverse a binary tree in-order (left, root, right) using recursion.
expected_explanation: This recursive function visits the left subtree first, then processes the current node, then visits the right subtree. The NULL check prevents infinite recursion and handles leaf nodes. In-order traversal of a binary search tree produces values in sorted order. Each recursive call operates on a smaller subtree.

title: String Substring Search
description: Find the first occurrence of a substring within a string.
expected_explanation: This function iterates through haystack, and for each position, attempts to match the entire needle string. The inner loop advances both pointers while characters match. If the inner loop reaches needle's null terminator, a match is found and the starting position is returned. Otherwise, haystack advances and tries the next position. Returns NULL if not found.
